mechanism_narrative: A declining federal funds rate trend consistently signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return direction is negative in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS is declining (measured over a 3-year rolling window), or the Rank IC falls below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 4.7% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 4.7% for two consecutive months, or the Rank IC is below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based contraction in consumer demand, which triggers a sell-off in equities as corporate revenue expectations are revised downward, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both decline in the latest month
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive in more than 55% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline in the same month, or the Rank IC is below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 (index base 2017=100) signals a supply shock that increases input costs and reduces corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is positive in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO < 100, or the Rank IC is below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the year-over-year CPI inflation rate above 3.0% signals persistent inflation that prompts the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive in more than 55% of instances when year-over-year CPIAUCSL > 3.0%, or the Rank IC is below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising trend in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) consistently signals strong labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return direction is negative in more than 55% of instances where PAYEMS is rising (measured over a 3-year rolling window), or the Rank IC falls below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) below its 12-month moving average signals a demand slowdown that reduces corporate revenue expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is positive in more than 55% of instances when GDPC1 < 12-month moving average, or the Rank IC is below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and year-over-year CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 3.0% signals a monetary policy tightening cycle in response to high inflation, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive in more than 55% of instances when both FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and year-over-year CPIAUCSL > 3.0%, or the Rank IC is below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.
